questions.question: Along which direction do equal spheres touch in a Body-Centered Cubic (BCC) unit cell, and what is the resulting packing efficiency?
questions.explanation: In BCC, the central sphere touches all $8$ corner spheres along the body diagonal, so $\sqrt{3}a = 4r$ with $2$ spheres per cell, giving $\pi\sqrt{3}/8 \approx 68.0\%$.

questions.question: In an FCC close-packed crystal with $N$ host spheres, how many octahedral and tetrahedral voids exist?
questions.explanation: In an FCC unit cell ($N=4$ spheres), there are $1 + 12/4 = 4 = N$ octahedral voids and $8 = 2N$ tetrahedral voids.

questions.question: What is the maximum radius ratio $r/R$ of a sphere fitting inside an octahedral void of host spheres of radius $R$?
questions.explanation: The octahedron of edge $2R$ has center-to-vertex distance $\sqrt{2}R$, so $R + r = \sqrt{2}R \implies r/R = \sqrt{2} - 1$.

questions.question: What is the densest lattice packing density of regular octahedra alone (Minkowski, 1904), and which polyhedra are the Voronoi cells of the BCC lattice?
questions.explanation: Regular octahedra achieve $18/19 \approx 94.7\%$ lattice packing density, while truncated octahedra are the space-tiling Voronoi cells of BCC.
